cost: THE RULING ASKS FOR A TERM HIS OWN RULING DELETED, and that is the first thing he should see. recal_85, verbatim: "Kill breadth and the tax". The tax it killed is described in compute_ovr.py to this day: "THE EMPTY-VOLUME TAX (recal_37/r40 era): subtracted up to 5 for heavy load at poor efficiency". This ruling asks for exactly five points subtracted from a card for heavy load at poor efficiency. It is the same term, on the same card class, at the same magnitude. recal_85 removed it because it was "the sole cause of every card printing BELOW its weaker end - 192 of them". Reinstating it in any form re-opens that, and the two rulings cannot both stand.

IT IS SEPARATELY INFEASIBLE, AND THIS ONE IS A PROOF RATHER THAN A SEARCH. RUSSELL WESTBROOK '17 is pinned at off 91 +-1 by recal_89. At the SAME volume (98 for both) he is WORSE than '15 on both faults the ruling names: efficiency 48 against 51, ball security 61 against 66. Any charge C(volume, efficiency, ball security) that is non-decreasing in volume and non-increasing in the other two - which every 'charge the inefficient, turnover-prone high-usage load' term is - therefore satisfies C('17) >= C('15). The ruling requires C('15) >= 3 printed points (90 -> 87 at the top of its band) while the pin requires C('17) <= 1. No such function exists. It is not a matter of parameters.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER: JAYLEN BROWN '26, pinned off 83 +-1 by recal_89, is efficiency 38 at volume 96 - THIRTEEN points worse than Westbrook '15 on the very quantity the charge reads. And a third: JAMES HARDEN '19, pinned 95 +-1, is ball security 62 at volume 99, more turnover-prone than Westbrook '15 at higher usage. Three of his own pins stand between this card and the number.

THE MEASURED FRONTIER, on the whole pool. The charge he asked for - K x volume x gate(volume 85->95) x gate(efficiency 60->40) x gate(ball security 75->55) - was swept: the largest size that breaks NO anchor is K = 0.04 and it is worth ONE printed point, Westbrook '15 90 -> 89. At K = 0.06 Westbrook '17 leaves his band; at 0.08 Jaylen Brown '26 leaves his too; and even at K = 0.14, with two of his pins broken, Westbrook '15 has only reached 87 - the very top of his target band. CLOSEST REACHABLE WITH EVERY ANCHOR HELD: 89.

THE RELIEF VARIANT WAS MEASURED TOO, and it trades one blocker for another. Relieving the charge by playmaking - so a creator's turnovers cost less - does protect Westbrook '17 (his playvol is 99 against '15's 93) and at full relief he holds 91 up to K = 0.30. But Jaylen Brown '26's playvol is 68, below any relief ramp, so he takes the charge undiminished and breaks at EVERY size: 80 at K = 0.10 against his 83 +-1. And Westbrook '15 still only reaches 89. Two variants tested, both fail, and the doctrine's cap of three is not needed - the third would have to gate on three-point range to separate the cards, which is not in his sentence and would be a per-player override wearing a formula's clothes.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT REACHABLE, stated so he can rule rather than be told no. Exactly one of these: (a) release RUSSELL WESTBROOK '17's 91 +-1 pin - it is the binding one, and it is arguably the same complaint, since '17 is the more inefficient and more turnover-prone season of the two; or (b) accept 89 rather than 85, which is one point and breaks nothing; or (c) re-open recal_85 and reinstate the empty-volume tax as a general term, accepting that 192 cards printed below their weaker end the last time it existed. This round takes none of them on its own authority.

NOTHING WAS HALF-APPLIED. o_score is byte-identical to the commit below this one: 0 cards move on OFF, DEF or OVR, no attribute moves, no anchor was superseded and no tax was re-ratified. The round is a measurement and a decline.

INDEPENDENCE FROM recal_109, as instructed: this round adds no term and touches nothing, so it survives a drop of the elite-passer round trivially. Westbrook is volume 98, which puts him at gate 0.00 of 109's term in any case.
notes: THE CARD. Russell Westbrook '15: volume 98, efficiency 51, ball security 66, playvol 93, 38.4% usage, 4.4 turnovers, .541 true shooting against a .576 era-relative mark, BPM 8.1. He prints OFF 90 and his ruling says 85.

WHY THE SHAPE HAD TO BE efficiency x ball security AT HIGH USAGE, and why that was still not enough. His sentence names two faults, and the second is what separates the class: Kobe Bryant '16 (efficiency 18) and Allen Iverson '02 (efficiency 32) are far more inefficient than Westbrook but CAREFUL - ball security 86 and 88 - and Carmelo Anthony '13 is 62 and 93. Westbrook '15 is the only card in the class that is poor at BOTH. That is why a charge on efficiency alone was never viable, and it is why the two-fault shape was the right instrument to test. It fails not on the class but on his own two Westbrook pins.

THE ONE INPUT THAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM, named and rejected. Westbrook '15 is three-point 38 against '17's 56 and Jaylen Brown '26's 54, so a charge that grows as outside range falls would catch him and spare both. It is rejected: 'cannot shoot threes' is not in his sentence, and a fourth gate tuned until exactly one card is caught is a per-player override, which doctrine 1 forbids however it is written.
MEASURED BEFORE DECLINING, and the lab reproduces the shipped board to zero mismatches before any change is applied, so every number above is a reading of the real pipeline rather than a model of it.
